title: Silk Roads: the handoffs
hook: Could distant trade work without one end-to-end traveler?

knows: Events happen in places and at different times.

objective: Follow the handoffs rather than imagining one highway.

claims.text: c. 1 CE: Eastern links. Han and Central Asian worlds exchange goods.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/trade-between-the-romans-and-the-empires-of-asia — Trade expansion, Parthian Stations, Merv, Ctesiphon, Palmyra and Antioch

claims.text: c. 1 CE: Branch point. Routes branch near Merv.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/trade-between-the-romans-and-the-empires-of-asia — Trade expansion, Parthian Stations, Merv, Ctesiphon, Palmyra and Antioch

claims.text: c. 1 CE: Mesopotamia. Trading posts connect overland and river routes.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/trade-between-the-romans-and-the-empires-of-asia — Trade expansion, Parthian Stations, Merv, Ctesiphon, Palmyra and Antioch

claims.text: c. 1 CE: Mediterranean. Caravan links reach eastern Mediterranean ports.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/trade-between-the-romans-and-the-empires-of-asia — Trade expansion, Parthian Stations, Merv, Ctesiphon, Palmyra and Antioch

claims.text: Follow the handoffs rather than imagining one highway. Trading posts stored and exchanged goods, and routes branched between rivers, caravan cities and ports. Goods could move far through this network without the map proving that one merchant traveled its entire length.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/trade-between-the-romans-and-the-empires-of-asia — Trade expansion, Parthian Stations, Merv, Ctesiphon, Palmyra and Antioch
